comments.note: Object.setPrototypeOf(this, new.target.prototype) is technically redundant for an ES2022 target since native class syntax handles instanceof correctly. It is harmless and defensively correct (protects against downstream transpilation by tsup or similar tools), so not a failure — just worth noting for Reviewer awareness.
exitCode is typed as readonly, preventing accidental mutation after construction. This is a good defensive practice.

summary: src/preflight.ts is a clean, well-implemented preflight module. PreflightError correctly extends Error with readonly exitCode, sets this.name, and restores the prototype chain via Object.setPrototypeOf (correct for a distributable library). checkNodeVersion() correctly parses process.versions.node and throws PreflightError with a helpful message.

One test quality observation (low priority): the 'includes the current version in error message' test uses a bare try/catch without expect.assertions(), creating a possible silent false-positive path. Not blocking — the throw is validated by a companion test. No fix-forward changes applied.

comments.note: Object.setPrototypeOf(this, new.target.prototype) in PreflightError constructor is the correct defensive practice for library code. Even though ES2022 native classes handle instanceof correctly, downstream consumers may bundle with tsup, Babel, or esbuild at a lower target. Leaving it in is the right call for a distributable library.

The 'includes the current version in the thrown error message' test uses a try/catch pattern without an assertion that the throw actually occurred. If checkNodeVersion(99) were to stop throwing, the test would silently pass (the catch block never executes). Prefer expect.assertions(2) at the top of the test body, or wrap with expect(() => ...).toThrow() and extract the error separately. Not blocking since the implementation is correct and the companion test ('throws PreflightError when required major version is very high') validates the throw independently.

afterEach(() => { vi.restoreAllMocks(); }) in tests/preflight.test.ts runs even though there are no vi.spyOn() calls in this file. This is valid defensive boilerplate (anticipates future mock additions) rather than dead code — leaving it is appropriate.
